newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sentrachem shrugs bln rand debt cut plan.
newsitem.headline: Sentrachem shrugs bln rand debt cut plan.

text.p: South African chemicals group Sentrachem Ltd's shares on Wednesday ignored the firm's restructuring plan announced on Tuesday to cut its debt by about one billion rand over the next 12 to 18 months.
By 1133 GMT Sentrachem shares lost 12 cents to 858 cents in light volume of nearly a 100,000 shares changing hands.
"Certainly the details that have been given are quite still. There's basically not enough to go on," one analyst who declined to be identified said.
The plan announced by Sentrachem's managing director John Job includes the merging of units National Chemical Products (NCP) and Karbochem into a larger and focused industrial chemical company.
Job said the group also planned go on with its plans to remove between 300 million and 350 million rand in working capital costs and the elimination of other costs.
But dealers said the plan lacked detail.

"They've announced this plan but there are no details as to how they'e going to go about it and I think that could be why nothing is happening in the share. It's good news but the market is still waiting to see how they are going to do this," one dealer said.

Sentrachem shares were hit by a disastrous first half-year where one-off charges of 261 million rand due to forward cover contracts and restructuring costs at its Sanachem unit plunged the group into loss.
But the shares staged a recovery from June 6 when the share price rose from 680 cents to a high of 890 cents on June 19 and dealers suspected the market could have known about the plan.
"It may well have leaked into the market beforehand because they have had a bit of a tick-up," one dealer said.
